title: wave start: an owner's landing-order answer does not order the wave

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
Observed 2026-11-11 (slicer wave 2): the spec check asked wave.parser-lazy-overlap ("Which order do s455, s456 and s451 land in?") and the owner answered 1, s455 first, so s456 and s451 are cut from it. `ork wave start slicer s455 s450 s456 s451 s453 --yes` then started s455 and s456 at the same time and queued s451 for the next slot (ork-20261111-213809-3951, -6e14); they were stopped by hand. `ork wave suggest` had already put s456 in a later wave than s455 because they share snapshot.py. Wanted: wave start honours the suggested wave layering and any recorded order answer: an item starts only after the items it is ordered behind have landed.

Re-anchored 2026-11-18:

- `startWave` in the daemon refuses members blocked by a slicer dependency (`blockedItems`, `internal/daemon/runs.go:1648-1681`; message "in this wave, not done", `BlockedMessage`, `internal/daemon/build.go:237-270`) and two engine slices (`internal/daemon/runs.go:1723-1738`). It does not read Files overlap; every other member is admitted at once and queued only for a slot (`internal/daemon/runs.go:1739-1750`; queue in `startQueuedLocked`, `internal/daemon/runs.go:2010`).
- adj 17 (`wave.selection`, suggested): ork warns when two items' Files overlap. The TUI Waves screen does (`internal/tui/waves.go`); `ork wave start` in the CLI does not (`internal/cli/wave.go:320-466` has no overlap read). The daemon already has the read: `slicer deps --overlap ID... --json` (`DepsOverlap`, `internal/slicercli/slicercli.go:43-51`; wire `wave.overlap`).
- adj 139 (`wave.start-input`, items): wave start takes the item ids the owner typed, not a stored suggestion, so the order of the typed list is the owner's order.
- An order answer filed in adj is free text against a question the spec check wrote; ork cannot turn it into an order in code. The Files overlap from slicer is data. This spec orders by overlap and the typed order, per adj 477 (`wave.overlap-order` = hold): a later member in the typed order waits until the earlier overlapping member lands.
- slicer computes overlaps and parallel sets (`slicer deps --overlap`, `slicer plan-parallel`) but does not start or hold runs; holding a run is ork's.

UI: `ork wave start` output gains a line per held member, and `ork status` shows the wait, so this slice gets a UI pass (rule u10).

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
Per adj 477 (hold). The fake slicer serves `deps --overlap` with pairs (s455, s456, shared `snapshot.py`) and (s455, s451, shared `snapshot.py`).

- `TestWaveStartHoldsAnOverlappingMemberBehindTheEarlierOne` in `internal/daemon/wave_test.go`: `wave.start` with s455, s450, s456, s451 starts s455 and s450; s456 and s451 are queued with `after: [s455]` and do not start when a slot frees. Red today: s456 starts with s455.
- `TestWaveHeldMemberStartsAfterTheEarlierLands` in `internal/daemon/wave_test.go`: when s455's run lands (final, slice done in the fake slicer), s456 starts, and s451 waits behind s456 only if they overlap. Red today: no hold.
- `TestWaveHeldMemberStaysWhenTheEarlierStops` in `internal/daemon/wave_test.go`: s455's run is stopped; s456 stays queued and `ork status` shows `waits on s455 (stopped)`. Red today.
- `TestWaveStartPrintsTheOrder` in `internal/cli/wave_test.go`: before the confirm, the text has `order: s456 after s455 (snapshot.py); s451 after s455 (snapshot.py)`. Red today: no line.
- `TestWaveStartWithoutOverlapIsUnchanged` in `internal/daemon/wave_test.go`: members with no shared path start as today. Green today (guard); mutation-check it by holding every member.

Added in the implementation (all green after the product code, each mutation-checked):

- `TestWaveStartSaysWhyAMemberIsHeld`, `TestWaveStartDoesNotHoldBehindAMemberThatDidNotStart`, `TestWaveOrderHoldsALaterMemberBehindEveryEarlierOverlap` and `TestWaitingOnNamesEachItemWhoseNewestRunHasNotLanded` in `internal/daemon/wave_test.go`.
- `TestWaveStartHeldMemberDoesNotResumeItsStoppedRun` in `internal/daemon/stoppedresume_test.go`.
- `TestWaveStartPrintsNoOrderLineWithoutOverlap` in `internal/cli/wave_test.go`; the CLI stubs that start a wave of two or more items now answer `wave.overlap`.

- `TestWaitingOnCountsAChainOfSliversAsItsParent` in `internal/daemon/wave_test.go` (fix round 1): an earlier member that runs as a sliver chain has runs named for its slivers; its last sliver stands for it, so a held member waits on it and starts once that sliver has landed.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Write the failing tests and see each red for the stated reason.
2. Per adj 477 (hold): in `startWave`, for two or more members, call `DepsOverlap`. For each pair with shared paths, the member later in the typed order is held behind the earlier one. Store the list on its run record (`after`), and admit it as queued.
3. `startQueuedLocked`: skip a queued run whose `after` list has a run that has not landed. A run that ended stopped or failed keeps its followers queued; the owner stops or retries them.
4. CLI: print the order line after the pair rule line and before the confirm; `--json` carries `after` on each item.
5. Do not parse adj answers for order; the typed order and slicer's overlap decide.
6. Docs: wave lifecycle in `docs/design.md` and the run record field in `docs/state.md`, citing the new record. Changelog entry with `slicer changelog add S342 --text "..."`.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
Acceptance criteria:
- A wave whose members share Files paths starts the earlier member in the typed order and holds each later one until the earlier one has landed.
- ork wave start prints the order before the confirm, naming the shared paths.
- A held member stays queued when the member it waits on stops or fails, and ork status says what it waits on.
- Members with no shared paths start as today.

Commands:
- `go test ./internal/daemon ./internal/cli -run 'TestWaveStart|TestWaveHeld' -v`
- `go vet ./...`
- `go test ./...`
- `gofmt -l .` prints nothing.
- `slicer check` exits 0.
- `adj lint` exits 0.
